camera.whyGame: A second trace in the animation graph will disagree with the aim trace about what the crosshair hit.

movement.plainEnglish: A pushed stick writes a sprint speed of 600. A stick that is not pushed writes 200. Motion matching builds a trajectory from that number. The aiming bool may pick an aim set. It is not a second speed.
movement.whyGame: If the camera graph also writes speed, whichever write lands last in the frame wins, and the gait flickers.

aoi.plainEnglish: A third-person mesh and its animation are expensive. Twice a second the authority traces and sets whether this pawn is relevant. Machines that are not relevant do not receive it.
aoi.whyGame: Writing that bool every frame, or from a client, either wastes the budget or hides pawns the player should still see.

ballistics.plainEnglish: Fire is its own button. A hit adds a small step of heat. Wear is the other float on the same weapon. The muzzle flash on the third-person mesh is local. It is not a replicated projectile. A miss adds no heat.
ballistics.whyGame: Adding heat while the player is only aiming makes the gun wear out from looking.

limbs.plainEnglish: Other players see the limp, so the limb is one server number. Any Damage starts the write, inside the authority check. A bruise stops at 10 percent of that limb's max. Crossing zero is the down. The number 90 in the sample is a stand-in.
limbs.whyGame: A client that subtracts so the limp appears early will snap, and a tick write injures the pawn while nobody hit it.

save.plainEnglish: The kit save stores limb floats, heat, wear, the magazine, the reserve, the equipped id, and vehicle fuel if there is a car. It does not store the motion-matching pose, the boom transform, or relevance. Load is Begin Play. Do not snapshot throttle in the middle of a gear change.
save.whyGame: A pose in the slot fights the animator, and a mid-gear throttle is not a finished fact.
